newsitem.title: USA: ADP posts record profits, revenues for 141st quarter.
newsitem.headline: ADP posts record profits, revenues for 141st quarter.

text.p: Automatic Data Processing Inc., one of the world's largest independent computing services firms, said Friday it achieved record profits and revenues for a 141st consecutive quarter.
ADP said net income for its fiscal first quarter, which ended Sept. 30, rose 14 percent to $93.3 million, or 32 cents a share, from $81.9 million, or 28 cents a share.
Revenue for the quarter expanded by 22 percent to $910.7 million from $747.1 million
Company President Arthur F. Weinbach said the company, based in Roseland, N.J., expected its double-digit revenue and earnings growth to continue for the rest of the fiscal year.
The company, which has more than 375,000 clients, also said that Russell P. Fradin, a senior partner of McKinsey & Co., will join ADP as senior corporate vice president, a newly created position.
Weinbach said Fradin would be responsible for ADP's overall strategic planning, including efforts to identify and pursue additional business opportunities beyond its current core businesses.
Fradin, who worked for McKinsey for 18 years, had been a leader of the firm's work in the information technology, telecommunications and transportation industries.
ADP's stock lost 50 cents to $42.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
